t: Lesson 4, Skills. Your instructor is Patrick Diamitani.
If you've explained a process three times, it should be a skill.
A skill teaches the agent one job, done your way.
It's a folder with one markdown file inside, called skill.md.
When a request matches, the agent loads it automatically.
At the top, a name and a description.
The description is how the agent decides when to use it.
Below that, the steps in plain language.
Skills scale because of progressive disclosure.
At first, the agent only sees the name and description.
The full steps load only when a request matches,
and long references live in separate files, read only when needed.
If a skill doesn't fire, the description is usually the problem.
Say what it does, say when to use it, and use the words people actually type.
The skill format is an open standard.
Put it in your project, keep it in your personal folder,
or add it in the Clawd app.
Write it once, and it travels with you.
Quick recap, a skill is a folder with a skill.
MD, and the description decides when it fires.
Your mission, turn the process you explain most often into your first skill.
Your know-how, packaged.
Next lesson, we connect the agent to your real tools.
